binIntro: Every sock in here is missing someone, and every one of them would like you to know they are handling it well.
locked: Someone in here is working up to saying something. Reunions to go: {n}.

pages.title: Oh. Hi.
pages.speaker: Left Argyle
body: Hello. Sorry, we don't get many visitors who aren't also socks. This is the Odd Bin. Everyone in here is missing someone, and everyone in here is handling it very well, thank you.
You just put two of us back together. We all watched. Nobody said anything, because it seemed private, but the fuzzy slipper cried a little lint.
So. Hi. We'll be here.

pages.title: Where We Went
pages.speaker: Polka Dot
body: We compared notes last night about where we went. It did not go well.
The dress sock says it spent a week inside a pillowcase. The baby sock says it went to a wedding in somebody's shoe. The knee high says it fell behind the radiator and saw things it won't discuss.
I was under the fridge, which I maintain is a real place. Nobody agreed on anything, except that it was nice to be asked.

pages.title: The Back
pages.speaker: Toe Sock
body: I have a theory, and five toes to count it on.
One: a dryer goes round. Two: anything that goes round has a back. Three: nobody has ever seen the back. Four: we have all been in the dryer. Five: some of us were in it, and then we weren't.
The dryer has a back. Everyone laughed, then everyone went quiet, and then the fuzzy slipper scooted a little closer to me, which I took as a yes.

pages.title: It's Fine
pages.speaker: The Tube Sock
body: I've been in here the longest. Two stripes, both still mostly red. People ask how I'm doing, and I say it's fine, because it is.
I have a good corner. The radiator reaches it in the mornings. I've watched every Reunion from here, and I cheer for each one out loud, which the others have asked me to stop doing.
I'm not waiting, exactly. I'm just here, in case. It's fine.

pages.title: A Different House
pages.speaker: Gray Crew
body: I came back last Load, and everyone keeps sniffing me. I understand. I smell like a different house.

Cedar, I think, and somebody else's soap, and a dog who was very good. I don't remember getting there. I remember a drawer that stuck, and a foot that ran cold, and a walk to the mailbox every morning.
I was looked after there. It was a nice house. This one is mine.

pages.title: The Vote
pages.speaker: Left Argyle
body: We held a vote, by a show of toes, on whether anyone should go looking for the back of the dryer.
Half the Bin voted to go. Half voted to wait. The baby sock voted twice, once each way, and we let it, because it was very sure both times.
The goers say you can't find what you don't look for. The waiters say someone has to be here when they come back. Both are right, so we're sleeping on it, in a pile, like always.

pages.title: Someone Went
pages.speaker: Polka Dot
body: The dress sock went. Thin, long, very brave. It climbed into the dryer while the door was open, wriggled toward the back, and was gone.
We waited a Load. Then ten. Nothing came back: not the dress sock, not a note, not even lint.
We don't think it's lost. We think it's somewhere with no door on our side. If you ever find a door on your side, we would very much like to hear about it.

pages.title: The Polite Ones
pages.speaker: Left Argyle
body: The new dryer hums in a key none of us has heard before, and today it opened on socks that belong to no one.

No drawer, no foot, no laundry day they can remember. One of them has a pattern none of us can name. They introduced themselves one at a time, apologized for the static, and asked, very politely, where they should wait.
We told them here was fine. They thanked us four times each.

pages.title: They Can Stay
pages.speaker: Gray Crew
body: We had a meeting about the strangers. It was short.
Someone asked where they came from. Someone asked if they would ever be matched. The strangers didn't know, and said sorry for not knowing.

I remember coming back smelling like a different house, and everyone scooting over anyway. So we scooted over. The strangers can stay. Nobody in here started out in here; that's sort of the point of the place.

pages.title: Two Lines
pages.speaker: The Tube Sock
body: It came out of the dryer wrapped in a towel, and I knew it before it landed.
I said it was fine for a very long time; now it actually is.

pages.title: The Map
pages.speaker: Toe Sock
body: I drew a map of the back of the dryer, in lint, on the floor of the Bin. It took most of a Load.
There's a river of warm air, a forest of lost hair ties, and a town where everyone is a left sock. North is wherever the dress sock went. I put a small x where I think it's having a nice time.
The strangers say it's wrong in about eleven places. Everyone looks at it anyway, every night, before we pile up.

pages.title: The Whole Thing
pages.speaker: Everyone in the Bin
body: We've been talking: the pairs in the Drawer, the ones still waiting, and the strangers, who apologized for interrupting.
We don't know where the back of the dryer goes. We don't know if everyone gets found. We do know someone kept opening the door, Load after Load, and turning each of us over to check.
We made you something for the wall. Also, something impossible came through the lint trap; it's yours.
You kept looking. That's the whole thing.
